subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in default-off session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after the sessions.activity contract lands, or should core stop at activity/diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards?
rationale: The request adds new core feature, config, alert delivery, UI/operator, privacy, and optional model-call behavior rather than repairing an established contract.

options.title: Keep downstream core design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/design item that follows the public sessions.activity API and defines a minimal built-in watchdog.

options.title: Route alerting to plugins
options.body: Limit core to public activity and diagnostics events, then let plugins, dashboards, or ClawHub packages own alert delivery and summaries.

options.title: Fold into visibility program
options.body: Use this only as context for broader run-progress and stall-recovery work, with a smaller canonical implementation issue before coding.

recommendation.title: Keep downstream core design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/design item that follows the public sessions.activity API and defines a minimal built-in watchdog.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has recent session-store work in the area and is a better routing candidate for the session contract boundary than an unrelated line-blame-only contributor.
